pencereler.0-5: This bridge tore itself apart in a forty mile an hour wind. The deck
pencereler.5-12: twisted like a ribbon, then dropped into the water. It had been open just four months. So how did
pencereler.12-20: a steady wind destroy solid steel? The wind made the deck flutter, and the flutter fed itself. Each twist pumped in more
pencereler.20-30: energy than the bridge could shed. One man escaped on his hands and knees. Every long bridge since is tested in a wind tunnel.

segmentler.metin: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge tore itself apart.
It took only a 40 mph wind.
So how could a 40 mph wind do this?
The answer is aeroelastic flutter — and it is why every major bridge is now wind-tunnel tested.
